newsitem.title: UK: Shell Expro to go ahead with Kingfisher oil/gas field.
newsitem.headline: Shell Expro to go ahead with Kingfisher oil/gas field.

text.p: Shell U.K. Exploration and Production said on Wednesday it had received British government approval for the development of its 220 million stg Kingfisher oil and natural gas field in the Central North Sea.
Shell Expro, operator in the U.K. sector of the North Sea for the Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Exxon Corp, said first production is expected late next year.
Production from the satellite field wil go by pipeline for processing and export via the nearby Brae Field, operated by Marathon.
Shell Export said more than 80 percent of the project expenditure will go to British companies supplying materials and services.
Located about 155 miles northeast of Aberdeen, Kingfisher consists of three seprate reservoirs, contains oil/condensate and gas and will be developed using six production wells, Shell Expro said.

Reserves are estimated at about 56 million barrels of oil and condensate and about 368 billion standard cibic feet of gas. Peak production levels are estimated at about 37,000 barrels per day pf condensate and 160 million standard cubic feet of wet gas a day.
Field life is estimated at about nine years, Shell Expro said.
The drilling programme wil bvegin late this year and continue until early 1999.
The oil/condensate export route comes ashore at Cruden Bay after pasisng through the Brae-Forties system. Gas exports will come ashore at St. Fergus.
